channel.title: Homestead Guides
channel.description: Free, research-backed homesteading how-tos for backyard homesteaders, sourced from university extension research.

item.title: Growing & Storing Potatoes: A Beginner's Guide to Seed Potatoes, Hilling & Curing for Winter
item.description: Real planting depth and spacing numbers, why chitting seed potatoes six weeks early can mean an earlier harvest, the hilling step that prevents green tubers, and the exact curing and storage temperatures from university extension potato research.

item.title: Fermented Pickles vs. Quick Pickles: A Beginner's Guide to Salt, Crunch & Safety
item.description: Why a fermented pickle and a quick vinegar pickle get their tang from two completely different processes, the brine temperature window that decides crunch vs. mush, and the fixes for soft, hollow, or scummy jars.

item.title: Winterizing a Beehive: A Beginner's Guide to Insulation, Moisture & Starvation Risk
item.description: Why trapped moisture, not cold, is what actually kills most overwintered colonies, the real hive-weight numbers to check, and when to treat for mites before the window closes.

item.title: Processing a Meat Rabbit at Home: A Beginner's Guide to Dressing, Dress-Out & Chilling
item.description: Real fryer age and weight targets, the actual dressing steps and dress-out percentages by breed, and why the carcass needs a 24-hour rest before you cut it.

item.title: Raising a Turkey for Thanksgiving: A Beginner's Guide to Timing, Feed & Processing Day
item.description: Why a Thanksgiving turkey's timeline starts months earlier than you'd think, real grow-out weeks by breed, the feed program, and how to chill a carcass safely to 40 F.

item.title: Harvesting & Extracting Honey: A Beginner's Guide to Knowing When and How
item.description: How to tell a frame of honey is actually ready to pull, crush-and-strain vs. extracting, and how much honey to leave for the bees to overwinter on.

item.title: Heating a Hunting Cabin Safely: A Beginner's Guide to Carbon Monoxide, Insulation & Condensation
item.description: Why an insulated overnight cabin carries a real CO risk a drafty blind doesn't, the heater mistakes that cause it, and how to insulate for warmth without sealing out the fresh air a heater needs.

item.title: Raising Meat Goats: A Beginner's Guide to Breeds, Feeding & Parasite Management
item.description: Boer vs. Kiko, the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio that prevents urinary calculi, realistic weaning and market weights, and the FAMACHA eye-check system for deworming.

item.title: Incubating & Hatching Chicken, Duck & Turkey Eggs: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Still-air vs. forced-air incubator temperatures, humidity, turning, candling at 8-12 days, lockdown, and what's normal (and what's not) on hatch day.

item.title: Home Dairy Basics: Making Cheese, Yogurt & Butter from Fresh Milk
item.description: Sanitation basics, why raw milk isn't recommended for home cheesemaking, the real temperatures for yogurt and an easy first cheese, and a no-equipment way to churn butter.

item.title: Firewood & Wood Heat for the Homestead: Seasoning, Stacking & Chimney Safety
item.description: How much wood you actually need, the moisture number that decides if it's ready to burn, safe stacking for airflow, and the chimney and carbon monoxide risks most people don't expect from wood heat.

item.title: Canning Meat, Poultry & Broth Safely at Home: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Hot pack vs. raw pack, exact headspace and processing times by jar size, and the prep steps that keep flavor good and botulism risk at zero.

item.title: Saving Vegetable Seeds for Beginners: Easy Crops, Isolation Distances & Storage
item.description: Which crops you can save seed from with zero isolation (peas, beans, lettuce, tomatoes), why hybrid seed won't come back true, real isolation-distance numbers, and how to store and test what you save.

item.title: Hardening Off Seedlings: A Beginner's Guide to Moving Transplants Outdoors Safely
item.description: The real 1-to-2-week daily schedule, which crops tolerate a light frost once hardened and which don't, and the signs that mean a plant needs more time indoors.

item.title: Safe Internal Temperatures for Homestead Meat & Poultry: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: The full USDA temperature chart (including rabbit and venison), exactly where to put the thermometer on each cut, how to calibrate one, and the danger-zone rule that matters as much as the number itself.

item.title: Preserving Fresh Eggs for Winter: A Beginner's Guide to Freezing, Water Glassing & What Not to Do
item.description: The freezing method extension services actually recommend, why water glassing isn't currently considered safe, and why a home dehydrator can't dry eggs properly.

item.title: Cooking in a Wood-Fired Oven: A Beginner's Guide to Pizza, Bread and Roasts on One Firing
item.description: One fire, a whole day of food: the temperatures and the order to cook in, from pizza at 650 F and up to bread under 500 F, plus how big a fire to build and when meat is safe.

item.title: Curing a New Cob Oven: A Beginner's Guide to the First Fires, Drying Time and Cracks
item.description: When to pull out the sand form, how to tell the dome is dry enough, why the first fires are small, and which cracks are normal and which mean you dried it too fast.

item.title: Testing Clay for a Cob Oven: A Beginner's Guide to the Jar, Ribbon and Test-Brick Checks
item.description: How to find out whether your own soil makes good cob before you build: the jar test for sand, silt and clay, the ribbon test for clay content, and why test bricks beat guessing.

item.title: Choosing a Cabin or Shed Building Site: A Beginner's Guide to Slope, Drainage & Rock
item.description: How to read slope, drainage, and depth-to-bedrock before you design a cabin or shed, and what changes about your foundation once the site turns out to be solid rock instead of soil — from West Virginia University and University of Nebraska–Lincoln Extension.

item.title: Building a Shed or Small Cabin by Yourself: A Beginner's Guide to Solo-Build Safety & Timing
item.description: The 50-pound lifting line, the ladder rules that replace having someone hold it, and the height where fall protection stops being optional even on a small roof — from OSHA, the University of Arizona, and Clemson University.

item.title: Building a Hunting Blind: A Beginner's Guide to Site Selection, Wind & Elevated Safety
item.description: Where to actually put a hunting blind (wind, thermals, concealment, and the property-line mistake that causes real conflict), plus the elevated-structure safety rules that matter most — from Missouri Department of Conservation, Mississippi State, Illinois, and Texas Parks & Wildlife.

item.title: Keeping Chickens Laying Through Winter: A Beginner's Guide to Light, Ventilation & Frostbite
item.description: Why hens stop laying when day length drops below 12 hours, the right way to add artificial light without stressing the flock, and the ventilation-not-insulation rule that actually prevents frostbite — from Penn State and Ohio State University Extension.

item.title: Canning vs. Freezing vs. Dehydrating: A Beginner's Guide to Choosing the Right Preservation Method
item.description: Which method keeps the most nutrients, which has the longest shelf life (it's not the one most people guess), equipment costs, and the safety line that matters more than preference — from University of Alaska Fairbanks Cooperative Extension.

item.title: Putting the Garden to Bed for Winter: A Beginner's Guide to Fall Cleanup, Cover Crops & Soil Testing
item.description: What to pull, bag, or compost before frost, the one fall cover crop beginners don't need to till under, when to soil test in autumn instead of spring, and the tool-care steps most gardeners skip — from Michigan State, Iowa State, and UConn Extension.

item.title: Raising Meat Chickens at Home: A Beginner's Guide to Broilers, Brooding & Processing
item.description: The brooding temperature curve that matters most in the first five weeks, real space-per-bird numbers, Cornish Cross vs. slower-growing breeds, and the feed-withdrawal window before processing day — from UVM, Oregon State, Missouri, Mississippi State, and Kentucky Extension.

item.title: Canning Tomatoes, Salsa & Sauce Safely at Home: A Beginner's Guide to Acidification
item.description: Exactly how much bottled lemon juice or citric acid each jar needs, why salsa recipes can't be improvised, and processing times by product and altitude — from Texas A&M AgriLife Extension and the National Center for Home Food Preservation.

item.title: Growing Zucchini & Summer Squash: A Beginner's Guide to Pollination, Blossom Drop & the Squash Vine Borer
item.description: How male and female squash flowers actually work, the hand-pollination fix for poor fruit set, and how to spot a squash vine borer before the plant wilts overnight — from University of Maryland, Illinois, and South Dakota State Extension.

item.title: Growing Cucumbers in a Backyard Garden: A Beginner's Guide to Trellising, Pollination & Bitterness
item.description: Real spacing and trellis numbers, how cucumber pollination actually works, and why bitter cucumbers are usually a watering problem, not a variety problem — from University of Maryland and Iowa State Extension.

item.title: Growing Peppers in a Backyard Garden: A Beginner's Guide to Spacing, Staking & Sunscald
item.description: Real transplant timing and spacing numbers, the difference between blossom drop and blossom-end rot, and the staking trick that cuts sunscald damage from 17% to under 2% — from Utah State, UC Cooperative Extension, and University of Maryland Extension.

item.title: Growing Mulberries in a Backyard Garden: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Which mulberry to plant (and which one is actually invasive), why a single tree may not fruit on its own, and how to harvest a tree that ripens over weeks instead of all at once — from NC State, Purdue, and University of Florida IFAS Extension.

item.title: Raising Coturnix Quail for Meat: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Real space, brooding-temperature, incubation, and feed numbers for backyard meat quail, plus the chilling and freezing steps that keep a home harvest safe — from Texas A&M AgriLife, Oklahoma State, Mississippi State, and Penn State Extension.

item.title: Jam & Pickle Ratios: A Beginner's Guide to the Fruit, Sugar, Vinegar & Salt Math
item.description: The tested fruit-to-sugar ratios for jam without added pectin, which fruits set on their own, and why a pickle brine's vinegar ratio is a safety line, not a flavor choice — from NCHFP and Penn State Extension.

item.title: Siting a Backyard Cabin Near a Tree: Root Zones, Foundations & Permits for Beginners
item.description: How to tell if a tree is healthy enough to build around, the root-zone math that decides how close you can dig, no-dig foundation options, and the permit/setback checks beginners skip — from Purdue Extension and the USDA Forest Service.

item.title: Growing Tomatoes in a Backyard Garden: A Beginner's Guide to Spacing, Staking & Blossom End Rot
item.description: Real spacing and planting-depth numbers, a fertilizing schedule that actually works, and the calcium/watering fix for blossom end rot — from UGA, University of Wisconsin, and Mississippi State Extension.

item.title: Aromatherapy at Home: A Beginner's Guide to Herbal Oils, Salves, and Candles from Your Own Land
item.description: Why aromatherapy is a gentle craft with real safety rules, the dilution numbers worth knowing, the dried-herb rule that prevents botulism risk, and what to gather on a northern homestead — from NCCIH, the Tisserand Institute, and Penn State Extension.

item.title: How to Build a Family Emergency Binder: Documents, Water Math & a Livestock Plan
item.description: What actually belongs in the binder, the water math most people get wrong, the power-outage food-safety clock, and the livestock evacuation plan most templates leave out — from Ready.gov, FoodSafety.gov, and USDA.

item.title: Frost Dates & Succession Planting: A Beginner's Guide to Timing Your Vegetable Garden
item.description: The exact weeks-before/after-frost chart by crop, and the two-week succession-planting rule that keeps a garden producing all season instead of all at once — from Purdue, Penn State, Missouri, and Maryland Extension.

item.title: Baking Bread at Home: Yeast, Sourdough & No-Knead for Beginners
item.description: The real temperature numbers for yeast bread, a 5-day sourdough starter timeline, the no-knead method, and which flour to reach for — from University of Kentucky, Clemson, Iowa State, and Arkansas Extension.

item.title: How to Label Your Pantry & Canning Jars: Dates, Shelf Life & Rotation Explained
item.description: What "best if used by" actually means, how long home-canned jars really last, real canned-goods storage times, and the FIFO system that keeps a pantry in order — from Penn State, Texas A&M AgriLife, and Utah State Extension.

item.title: Winterizing the Homestead: A Beginner's Checklist for Animals, Pipes & Power
item.description: How much more chickens eat and drink in the cold, the cattle energy rule that surprises most beginners, frozen-pipe prevention, and safe generator placement — from NC State, UGA, Oklahoma State, and CDC.

item.title: Building a Wood-Fired Cob Oven: A Beginner's Guide to Earthen Oven Construction
item.description: The three layers that actually make a cob oven work, the door-height rule that decides how well it drafts, a safe curing-fire schedule, and clearance-to-combustibles basics.

item.title: Building a Chicken Tractor: A Beginner's Guide to Mobile Coops
item.description: Real space numbers for broilers vs. layers, why the daily move matters, and the predator-proofing details a lightweight pen actually needs — from Oregon State Extension and the Government of Alberta.

item.title: Fermenting Vegetables at Home: A Beginner's Guide to Sauerkraut & Pickles
item.description: The tested salt ratios, fermentation temperature and time, and the real signs that tell you a batch went wrong — from the National Center for Home Food Preservation and university extension.

item.title: Composting Toilets for Off-Grid Living: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: How a composting toilet actually works, the carbon and moisture balance that keeps it from failing, why most home units can't fully sterilize waste, and the legal checks to make before you install one — from Washington State DOH, West Virginia University, and the EPA.

item.title: Building a Backyard Chicken Coop: A Beginner's Guide to Space, Nest Boxes & Predator-Proofing
item.description: Real square-footage numbers for coop and run space, nest box and roost sizing, and the predator-proofing details (hardware cloth, buried wire aprons) that actually keep a flock safe — from Penn State and Oregon State Extension.

item.title: Building Your Own Beehive: A Beginner's Guide to Langstroth Hive Construction
item.description: Box dimensions, bee space, materials, weatherproofing, and hive-stand siting for building a Langstroth beehive from scratch — with real numbers from extension and apiary-association sources.

item.title: Building a Goat & Sheep Loafing Shed: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: How much shed space goats and sheep actually need, how to site a three-sided loafing shed, and the bedding and feeder-space numbers that keep a small flock or herd healthy — from university extension research.

item.title: Growing a Backyard Berry Patch: Blueberries, Strawberries & Raspberries for Beginners
item.description: The soil-pH mistake that kills blueberries for good, how to pick the right strawberry type for your space, and the raspberry pruning rule that decides whether you get a crop this year — from Penn State, Oregon State, and University of Minnesota Extension.

item.title: Home Food Dehydrating for Beginners: Drying Fruits, Vegetables & Jerky Safely
item.description: The real temperature to dry at, why fruit needs a dip first, the storage step most beginners skip, and the one extra safety step jerky needs that vegetables don't — from NCHFP, Penn State, and USDA.

item.title: Season Extension for Your Garden: Hoop Houses vs. Cold Frames for Beginners
item.description: A cold frame nudges your harvest a few weeks either direction; a hoop house can add two months on each end of the season. How to tell which one your garden actually needs, from Oklahoma State, Iowa State, and NC State Extension.

item.title: Smoking & Curing Meat at Home: A Beginner's Guide to Safe Ham, Bacon & Sausage
item.description: Why the cure, not the smoke, is what actually makes cured meat safe — exact ratios, curing time by thickness, and why beginners should master hot smoking before ever trying cold smoking.

item.title: Keeping a Family Milk Cow: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Jersey or Holstein, how much land and barn space a cow actually needs, real water/hay numbers, and why the dry period before calving matters — from university extension research.

item.title: Rainwater Harvesting for the Garden: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: How much water your roof actually collects, first-flush diverters, safe storage tank materials, and how to use harvested rain safely on food crops — from EPA and university extension research.

item.title: Backyard Composting for Beginners: Turn Scraps Into Rich Garden Soil
item.description: The real carbon:nitrogen ratio, browns vs. greens, the pile size that actually heats up, and how to fix a smelly or cold pile — sourced from Oregon State, Washington State, and Cornell.

item.title: How to Start Raising Sheep at Home: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Wool breed or hair breed, the fencing that actually holds a sheep, the copper mineral trap that can kill a flock, and lambing basics — from university extension research.

item.title: Root Cellar Storage for Beginners: How to Keep Your Harvest All Winter
item.description: No canning jar required: learn the real temperature/humidity zones, curing steps, and storage life for potatoes, onions, carrots, squash, and more, from university extension research.

item.title: How to Raise Pigs for Meat at Home: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Thinking about raising a feeder pig or two for the freezer? Learn real space, fencing, feed-by-weight, temperature, and timeline numbers from university extension research.

item.title: How to Start an Herb Garden: A Beginner's Guide to Growing, Harvesting, and Drying Herbs
item.description: Thinking about growing your own herbs? Learn sun and soil needs, the easiest herbs to start with, correct watering, and how to harvest and dry a real harvest, from university extension research.

item.title: How to Start Raising Backyard Turkeys: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Thinking about raising turkeys? Learn broad-breasted vs. heritage breed choice, brooder temperature schedules, space by age, and the one rule that keeps turkeys and chickens apart, from university extension research.

item.title: How to Start Raising Backyard Dairy Goats: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Thinking about keeping dairy goats? Learn breed choice, housing and fencing, feeding and the copper mineral trap, and kidding timing from university extension research.

item.title: Home Canning for Beginners: Water-Bath vs. Pressure Canning Explained
item.description: A beginner's guide to safe home canning: why acidity decides water-bath vs. pressure canning, jar/lid prep, headspace, and altitude adjustments, from university extension sources.

item.title: How to Raise Meat Rabbits at Home: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Thinking about raising rabbits for meat? Learn cage size by weight, feeding amounts, breeding and kindling timing, and health warning signs from university extension research.

item.title: Companion Planting for Vegetable Gardens: What Actually Works
item.description: Which companion planting pairings are backed by real research, and which are garden folklore? A beginner's guide to what to plant together — and what to keep apart.

item.title: How to Start Beekeeping: Beginner Guide to Your First Hive
item.description: Thinking about your first beehive? Learn hive types, how to get bees, startup costs, the first-year calendar, and varroa mite basics from extension research.

item.title: How to Start Raising Backyard Ducks: Beginner Guide
item.description: Thinking about backyard ducks? Learn breed choice, brooder temperatures, water requirements, and feed-by-age numbers before your ducklings arrive.

item.title: How to Start a Backyard Chicken Flock: Beginner Guide
item.description: Starting backyard chickens? Learn coop space, brooder temps, feed types by age, predator-proofing, and when you'll get your first eggs.

item.title: How to Start a Backyard Apple Orchard: Beginner's Guide
item.description: Planning your first apple orchard? Learn chill hours, pollination, rootstock spacing, and planting steps every beginner needs.
